RagShortTexts: Piast partitions create several centers of power.
Succession depends on kinship, recognition and effective strength.

Variants.Content: Piast relatives hold lands and followers in different duchies. Succession combines kin precedence, local recognition and control of castles. Revenues and guards sustain allotted rights; marriages and compromises reduce conflict while creating further claims.
Related princes may issue opposing orders. Garrison holders need credible provision and backing; changing a banner is easier than restoring supplies after neighboring support is lost.
Partition concerns revenues, retainers and marriage promises as well as boundaries. Concessions can prevent war but need authority over local disputes and arrears defined.
Households fear rival rent demands on the same land. Witnesses and agreements help; traders must learn which guarantor a changed checkpoint recognizes.
